19_reproducibility.hypothesis: The frozen C2 pipeline's OOF probabilities, regenerated via cross_val_predict on the exact winning config D pipeline with the frozen skf2_folds.json splits, should reproduce c2_summary.json's cv_M2 to floating-point precision.
19_reproducibility.result: Reproduced pooled M2@0.5 = 0.679430990462764 vs frozen cv_M2 = 0.679431 (abs diff = 9.5e-09).
19_reproducibility.conclusion: Confirmed -- the frozen C2 result is exactly reproducible from the saved fold indices and pipeline definition; h7_control_oof.csv now holds genuine per-row OOF probabilities for C2 (never saved before, since the original ablation only kept hard predictions).

20_threshold_optimization.hypothesis: A pooled-OOF threshold sweep (0.10-0.90) may find a threshold that beats 0.50 on Macro-F2/M2.
20_threshold_optimization.result: Best threshold = 0.54, M2 = 0.7064 vs M2@0.50 = 0.6794 (gain = 0.0270). The gain comes from fewer false positives (50->35) but MORE false negatives (77->90) on the 'Applicable' class.
20_threshold_optimization.conclusion: The metric gain is real but modest (+0.027 M2), and raising the threshold trades recall on the safety-critical 'Applicable' class for precision -- directly opposed to CLAUDE.md's stated principle that false negatives (missing an applicable subsection) are the costlier error. Decision: keep the frozen 0.50 threshold for the actual submission; document 0.54 as a quantified alternative, not adopted.

21_threshold_stability.hypothesis: If the pooled-optimal threshold is a real signal (not overfit to the pooled OOF), per-fold optimal thresholds should cluster near it.
21_threshold_stability.result: Per-fold optimal thresholds: [0.64, 0.50, 0.54, 0.53, 0.51], mean=0.544, median=0.53, std=0.056, range=0.14.
21_threshold_stability.conclusion: Reasonably stable for 4 of 5 folds (0.50-0.54), but fold 0 is an outlier requiring 0.64 -- consistent with, and reinforcing, the decision in 20.0 to keep the frozen 0.50 threshold rather than commit to a single tuned value.

22_feature_ablation.hypothesis: Cumulatively adding C2's structural/demographic/negation numeric features on top of TF-IDF text should improve pooled OOF M2 over text alone.
22_feature_ablation.result: Text only M2=0.6819 > Structural M2=0.6732 > +Demographics M2=0.6720 < +Negation/Full M2=0.6794. Negation recovers most, but not all, of the dip introduced by the structural+demographic features; Full C2 == +Negation exactly (both use the same 4 numeric features + gender).
22_feature_ablation.conclusion: Not confirmed as stated -- on this dataset and fold split, the engineered numeric/demographic features are pooled-OOF-neutral-to-slightly-negative for a linear model once TF-IDF already captures most lexical signal; negation_count is the one engineered feature that clearly pulls its weight. This does not mean the features are useless (see 25.0's subgroup findings and 23.0's coefficient magnitudes) -- it means their contribution is concentrated in specific subgroups rather than a uniform pooled lift.

23_feature_importance.hypothesis: Grouping the frozen model's LogisticRegression coefficients by category should show which feature families the model actually relies on.
23_feature_importance.result: By mean |coefficient|: protocol length (0.550) > negation (0.283) > structural (0.231) > clinical terms (0.217) > lexical (0.105) > demographics (0.092). No ICD-10 features exist in C2's feature set at all -- C2 never extracted ICD-10 as an engineered feature (only the H6 T4 transformer variant added it).
23_feature_importance.conclusion: The single engineered numeric features (protocol_len, negation_count, has_structured_header) carry disproportionately large individual coefficients compared to any single TF-IDF term, consistent with 22.0's finding that negation is the most load-bearing engineered feature; demographics (age/gender) carry the smallest average weight of any category.

24_error_analysis.hypothesis: C2's errors at threshold 0.50 should fall into recognizable categories (negation, age/gender contradiction, severity/comorbidity, missing information, ambiguous wording, annotation ambiguity).
24_error_analysis.result: 50 FP / 77 FN out of 690 rows (Precision(1)=0.883, Recall(1)=0.830, Precision(0)=0.708, Recall(0)=0.789, Macro-F2=0.8057). 10 representative examples categorized: 2 ambiguous wording, 2 severity/comorbidity, 3 missing information, 2 age/gender contradiction with probable annotation ambiguity, 1 missing information-with-ambiguity.
24_error_analysis.conclusion: No standalone negation-miss category emerged in this sample (negation_count is already an explicit, comparatively well-used feature per 23.0); the two hardest FN cases (ids 525, 126/127) are the same demographic-contradiction-yet-labeled-Applicable rows independently found in the H6 T3/T4 error analysis, reinforcing that these are dataset-level labeling edge cases rather than model-specific failures.

25_subgroup_analysis.hypothesis: Performance should degrade for very long protocols and for rows missing key structured fields (age/gender/ICD).
25_subgroup_analysis.result: Protocol length: Q4 (longest) macro_f2=0.768, the worst quartile (Q3 best at 0.826). Age missing (n=12): macro_f2=0.357, M2=0.0 -- a severe, if small, weak subgroup. Gender missing and ICD missing are the *same* 193 rows (both come from the same structured-header block being absent) and both score macro_f2=0.725 vs 0.820 when present.
25_subgroup_analysis.conclusion: Confirmed -- long protocols and rows lacking the structured header (which removes gender/ICD/age-reliability together, not independently) are measurably harder; the 12 age-missing rows are a small but severe blind spot worth flagging as a limitation rather than a fixable bug given the sample size.

decision.threshold: Tiny/borderline gain (+0.027 M2) that trades recall for precision on the safety-critical class -> keep the frozen 0.50 threshold for the submission.
decision.features: Feature ablation shows C2's gain over plain TF-IDF is small and concentrated in negation_count; the numeric/demographic block as a whole is pooled-OOF-neutral but measurably helps specific subgroups per 25.0 -- keep all features (no evidence they hurt, some evidence of subgroup-specific value, and CLAUDE.md explicitly asks for medical-domain feature engineering to be demonstrated).
decision.overall: C2 remains frozen and unchanged as the Stage 2 submission model; H7 is a validation/analysis layer only, not a new candidate architecture.
